prerequisites: Ability to read and understand documentation written in English (recommended).

learning_outcomes.text: Ability to apply methods of information theory, adaptive modulation, and channel coding, as well as advanced digital signal processing techniques to communication and audiovisual systems.
Interpret, analyze and apply methods of information theory in data transmission.
Interpret, analyze and apply error control methods through noisy transmission channels.
Compare different error control codes and analyze their performance in communication systems.
Apply interleaving techniques to improve performance against bursts.
Design coding and decoding systems based on convolutional codes, turbo codes and LDPC.
Justify advanced error control techniques used in current wired and wireless telecommunication systems.
Analyze multi-layer error control systems for multimedia communications in wireless networks.
Analyze multi-layer error control systems in wireless sensor and ad-hoc networks.
Design and compare signal discrimination systems using low cross-correlation sequences.
Perform group work tasks to apply information theory and channel coding methods in telecommunication systems.

syllabus_topics: Coding of discrete information sources. Data compression algorithms
Applications of error control codes in current telecommunication systems
Optimal data compression algorithm based on Huffman
Barker codes and Golay codes in noisy environments
Design of a complete data transmission system with error detection and correction

assessment_methods.method: Group work, contribution tracking, report submission and oral defense

assessment_rules: To pass the course in the ordinary call, all four parts (group work, individual work, lab practices, final test) must be satisfactorily passed. The final grade is calculated as: 0.2 * Group work + 0.1 * Individual work + 0.3 * Lab practices + 0.4 * Final test. Group and individual assignments can only be completed in the ordinary call. For the extraordinary call, approved group and individual work from the ordinary call will be considered, otherwise, the grade will be 0. Lab practices from the ordinary call, if approved, will keep their grade; otherwise, a lab exam with a minimum score of 5 out of 10 must be passed. A final knowledge test with a minimum score of 5 out of 10 must also be passed. The final grade for the extraordinary call is calculated as: 0.4 * Final test + 0.3 * Lab practices + 0.3 * Assignments grade. For differentiated evaluation, a final exam on theoretical and practical content will be conducted, with the final grade calculated as: 0.7 * Final theory test + 0.3 * Final practical test.
